newsitem.title: UK: Graseby says U.S. defence dept hikes order.
newsitem.headline: Graseby says U.S. defence dept hikes order.

text.p: British electronic instruments group Graseby Plc said on Monday that the U.S. Department of Defence had increased the value of one of its production orders placed with the company to $77 million from $56 million.

Graseby said the department had increased the value of its chemical agents detection systems programme known as ACADA (Automatic Chemical Agent Detector and Alarm) which was originally placed in July 1996.
"Graseby anticipates that further international requirements will generate significant additional business over the same time period," the company said.
It said the U.S. department had already exercised their intitial production option for the programme valued at $18 million.
"Delivery of these production units will commence in the second half of 1997," it said.

Peter Lester, Graseby's chief executive said, "This is a substantial increase which recognises the need for more units by the DOD. Future prospects for sales of our equipment to other countries are also looking very encouraging".
The company's share price was up 4 1/2 pence to 151p in declining market.
